_note: Full-inventory calibrated parameters. ADOPTED 2026-07-16: chi2 objective at the corrected softwood reference (5-5 = 4.0, 4-O-5 = 1.0 per 100 C9). Source: results/calibration_full.log + mini_forward_full_calibrated.csv (commit 8bf3fee). Mean RMSE 1.61 pts (softwood 0.98, poplar 1.19, high-S 2.66); scores sse 0.00574 / chi2 25.44.
_supersedes: Replaces the sse fit at the retired reference (softwood 5-5 = 12.0, 4-O-5 = 4.0): k_bo4 8.0, k_bo4_nuc 1.0898, k_b5 2.8659, k_b1 0.2792, k_bb 5.8624, k_55 2.088, k_4o5 0.298, n_nuclei 5.2851. That reference had no traceable provenance (see calibrate_full.py and ../Lignin_BioChem docs/01 Exp 10); the sse objective assumed every linkage measured to the same ABSOLUTE precision, which is false. Both were retired the same day. The sse fit at the CORRECTED reference (k_bo4_nuc 2.2031, k_bb 12.2076, n_nuclei 2.7598; mean RMSE 1.90) is kept as the sensitivity check in calibration_full_sse.log.
_why_chi2: chi2 weights each linkage by its estimated measurement sigma; sse weights by absolute magnitude, so beta-O-4 (60-89% of linkages) dominates and 4-O-5 (0.6-1.5%) is ignored. At the corrected reference chi2 wins on BOTH metrics -- including sse's own (sse 0.00574 vs 0.00663) -- which means the sse fit was not at its own global optimum but had overfit the fitting-stage replicate noise. chi2 also generalises better (LOOCV mean 3.4 vs 3.8 pts) and closes beta-beta (z = -0.29/-1.57/-1.01 vs sse's -1.99/-3.14/-2.58). See calibrate_full.PRIMARY_OBJECTIVE.
_k_bo4_nuc_WARNING: k_bo4_nuc = 0.9213 sits almost exactly on the ~0.9 the Gani monomer-monomer barriers imply (beta-O-4 6.3 vs beta-beta 5.2 kcal/mol). DO NOT read that as corroboration -- the claim that it does was WITHDRAWN 2026-07-16 (generator 4d86d80). The linkage inventory barely determines this constant: it returns 2.2031 under sse at this same reference (the OBJECTIVE alone swings it 2.4x), 1.59-3.48 across the defensible reference range (Exp 10), and a 2000-fold sweep of it moves the modelled inventory by at most 2.5 sigma of simulator noise against 13-35 sigma for the other five constants (Exp 12). Three knobs, three swings; one of them happens to land near 0.9. Report the value; draw nothing from where it lands.
_nucleation: k_bo4_nuc is beta-O-4 at the MONOMER-MONOMER step, fitted separately from the chain-extension k_bo4 because nucleation is a different reaction -- the DFT barriers put beta-O-4 middling at that step where it dominates chain extension. That MECHANISTIC claim stands and is supported by a matched ablation (single-phase, own 7 params, 5.2x worse) rather than by the fitted value; see _k_bo4_nuc_WARNING. bb_s_boost (a flat x4 fudge on S-S beta-beta) was REMOVED 2026-07-15 and replaced by Gani's pair specificity (mini_forward_generator._pair_mod). RETRACTED from this note 2026-07-16: 'Its fitted value (1.09) independently lands near the Gani-implied ~0.9 -- a check that the chemistry, not the fit, is setting it', and 'beta-beta now rises monotonically with S/G as an emergent consequence'. At this calibration beta-beta's MAGNITUDE is fit (3.5 vs 3.8 at softwood) but its S/G trend is not: measured p_bb per nucleation event is 0.830/0.835/0.840 across S/G 0/1/3 -- flat, because at k_bb = 16.78 beta-beta already wins ~83% of nucleation events at softwood and cannot exceed 1. The emergence mechanism is real but saturated out at this fit. See ../Lignin_BioChem docs/01 Exp 13.
_ceiling: Because the model emits ONE 120-unit molecule, total bonds = n_target - 1 = 119 regardless of composition, and beta-beta forms only at nucleation. So beta-beta% = p_bb * n_nuclei / 119 exactly. At n_nuclei = round(4.716) = 5 the maximum attainable beta-beta is 5/119 = 4.20%, reached only if EVERY nucleation event yields a resinol. Poplar's reference beta-beta (5.13%) is therefore UNREACHABLE IN PRINCIPLE at this fit (would require p_bb = 1.22); high-S's 4.57% requires 1.09. Implied nuclei: softwood 5.39, poplar 7.31, high-S 6.47 -- one integer must serve all three and it serves softwood. This is why the residual beta-beta deficit is largest at poplar. Exp 13.
